title: Visitor car parking, 5 or more dwellings: 0.1 bays per dwelling (Location A) or 0.15 (Location B), rounded up (Table 3.9)
text: Table 3.9 Visitor car parking: 0-4 dwellings - No visitor parking required; 5+ dwellings - 0.1 bays per dwelling (Location A), 0.15 bays per dwelling (Location B). (1) Calculations of parking ratios shall be rounded up to the next whole number.

replaces.note: 1 per 4 dwellings to 12, then 1 per 8 (A and B alike) -> 0-4 nil; 0.1 (A) / 0.15 (B) per dwelling

notes: Register C4P2-100 (0-4 dwellings: none, relaxed), C4P2-101 (Location A relaxed: 12 -> 2, 40 -> 4, 100 -> 10), C4P2-102 (Location B mixed: 12 -> 2, 40 -> 6, 100 -> 15, 200 -> 30; lower than Vol 2 up to about 60 dwellings, higher above). Table 3.9 footnote 1: rounded up to the next whole number (round(x + 0.4999) is ceiling for these ratios). diverges: ch4p1 Table 2.3a rounds to the nearest whole number for the same rates (register C4P2-104). Footnote 2 (one car bay less per five motorcycle bays) is not applied to visitor bays: the table does not say which bays it reduces. The required bay count comes from table-3.9-visitor-bays, keyed on site.location (rows A and B only): an unknown location gives CANNOT_TELL, where the earlier 'A else B' formula treated any value other than 'A' as Location B.
